column2: 4.1. Strategic awareness

Do you have a definition of open data reuse in your country?
 
For Explanation:
* If yes, please specify it.
column4:
The Italian legislation expressly provides for the definition of reuse of open data in the Digital Administration Code - legislative decree 82/2005 - Article 1, paragraph n-bis), where reuse means "use of the data referred to in Article 2(1)(e) of legislative decree no. 36 of 24 January 2006";
 [ https://www.normattiva.it/uri-res/N2Ls?urn:nir:stato:decreto.legislativo:2005-03-07;82 ]
The provision refers back to the definition contained in turn in Legislative Decree 36/2006 on the transposition of the PSI Directive, as subsequently amended by  the Legislative Decree 200 of 8 November 2021 transposing the Open Data Directive. Specifically:
(e) re-use: the use by natural or legal persons of documents held by: 
      (1) public administrations or bodies governed by public law for commercial purposes or for non-commercial purposes other than the institutional purposes for which the documents were produced, with the exception of except for the exchange of documents between public administrations or bodies governed by public law, or between administrations and bodies governed by public law, carried out exclusively within the framework of the performance of the institutional tasks of which they are holders; 
      (2) public undertakings and private undertakings referred to in Article 1, paragraph 2-quater, for commercial purposes or for non-commercial purposes other than those relating to the provision of services of general interest general interest services for which the documents have been produced, with the exception of for the exchange of documents between public undertakings and public administrations or bodies governed by public law set up exclusively within the framework of the performance of the tasks institutional tasks of the public administrations 
 [ https://www.normattiva.it/uri-res/N2Ls?urn:nir:stato:decreto.legislativo:2006-01-24;36~art2-com1-lete  ]

column7:
The processes are conducted at public body level, such as at regional level. 
Some examples:
The Open Data portal of the Emilia Romagna Region provides an online form to collect information about the re-use made of the data (https://dati.emilia-romagna.it/?q=contact/Segnala-un-uso-dei-dati);
Lombardia Region collects information about the cases of re-use of the datasets published in the regional data portal (https://www.dati.lombardia.it/Government/Utilizzo-dei-dataset/m58v-fh6e/data);
The public undertaking TPER publishes a list of apps developped by reusing open data made available (https://www.tper.it/apps).

On the portal dati.puglia.it there are  statistics about the datasets published, in the statistics section [most downloaded resources, most viewed resources, etc.]. Moreover, in order to monitor the level of reuse of open data, the https://odlab.regione.puglia.it/ section has been developed, which can always be accessed from the single regional open data portal dati.puglia.it, and which contains testimonials on regional open data reuse projects.

The portal dati.toscana.it is monitored through the platform Web Analytics Italia with statistics on access and download.

The use and impact of open data are included in a specific section of the annual report "The ICT spending in the Italian PA", see https://www.agid.gov.it/sites/default/files/repository_files/_la_spesa_ict_2021_nella_pa_italiana_-_principali_trend_e_percorsi_in_atto_final_v.02_2.pdf
This report is also linked to the Three-Year Plan for ICT in the PA that includes specific actions on data and open data. The implementation of those actions is annually measured and monitored, see  https://monitoraggiopianotriennale.italia.it/                                                                                                                                                                                           In the first report described, regarding the impact of Open Data, the paragraph 4.3 Data Governance e Open Data describes how the availability of open data in central and local government supports web and mobile application development activities. Development activities on open format datasets are very varied. In particular, it highlights the development of vertical applications (for the management of building sites, state property, etc.), and dashboard solutions enabling the analysis of real-time data (traffic, infomobility, weather, territory and environment) and of data at regional and municipal level (labour, expenditure, health, housing market). As can be seen from the graphs, a comparison was made between the extent of the release of datasets in open format and the development of services and applications based on the released data.
The second link indicated relates specifically to the monitoring of the objectives defined in the Three-Year Plan, and provides in open format all data related to this monitoring. The analysis of the rates of achievement of the objectives allows the comparison needed to analyse the impact of open data on digital services and any other aspect of interest.

column4:
A series of meetings, as part of the Forum PA's Cantieri project, involving stakeholders from both civil society and government,  addressing the issues from the point of view of reusers and public and private entities engaged in impact measurement initiatives:
14/6/2022 – “Open data and interoperability: enhancing PA information assets to enable the once-only principle”. Full interoperability of public datasets is one of the main objectives pursued by the strategies for digital PA, including through the resources provided by the NRP. Specifically, the Plan aims to overcome vertical silos that are not interconnected through the implementation of the Digital National Data Platform (PDND) and the central catalog of APIs for accessing information held by public bodies. In this talk dedicated to the topic of data governance in the public sphere, we will delve into the challenges that await PAs as part of the path to implementing the data and interoperability measures envisaged by the NDPND, listening to the experience of some of the main administrations involved and the technology companies that are proposed as enablers of this important process. https://www.forumpa.it/manifestazioni/forum-pa-2022/dati-pubblici-e-interoperabilita-valorizzare-il-patrimonio-informativo-della-pa-per-abilitare-il-principio-once-only/ 

14/6/2022 “Replicability of an Italian good practice in Europe: Open Data, Civic Monitoring and Cohesion Policies in Schools”. A Scuola di OpenCoesione (ASOC) is an innovative digital education pathway aimed at promoting and developing principles of active and aware citizenship in Italian schools through research activities and civic monitoring of European and national public funding, to answer the fundamental question, "How is public money spent in the territories?" ASOC makes it possible to introduce in schools the themes of civic monitoring, active citizenship, and participation, through an educational model structured by phases and moments of confrontation. A model that has become a point of reference in national and European cohesion policies, so much so that it has been successfully transferred and replicated in several EU countries, and recently put at the center of new experimentation also in the context of European Territorial Cooperation.
https://www.forumpa.it/manifestazioni/forum-pa-2022/replicabilita-di-una-buona-pratica-italiana-in-europa-open-data-monitoraggio-civico-e-politiche-di-coesione-nelle-scuole/

https://open.gov.it/governo-aperto/piano-nazionale/5nap/monitoraggio
The Fifth National Action Plan for Open Government 2022 - 2023 (5NAP https://open.gov.it/sites/default/files/media/documents/2022-09/I%20REPORT%20VALUTAZIONE%205NAP_FINALE.pdf  ) is the result of a co-creation process, carried out in line with the OGP Standards, in which different levels of government - central and regional - and organised civil society collaborated to define a few but significant commitments, in line with the recommendations of the IRM (Indipendent Reporting Mechanism) to make the implementation of open government principles more widespread and the impact of policies more impact of policies based on these principles.
In the evaluation and monitoring section, updates are provided on the status of implementation of the actions and commitments contained in the Plan.
The teams responsible for implementing the commitments progressively feed the monitoring system with data on the activities carried out, according to the scheduled timetable and, for each activity, provide evidence supporting the results/products achieved.
On the basis of this monitoring, four-monthly evaluation reports are produced, which highlight the progress of the Plan as a whole and can be consulted here.
A timeline provides monthly access to the monitoring and evaluation data and reports.
It is also possible to find out about the progress of activities by viewing the indicators, target values and the outcome in terms of results achieved by each commitment in the Plan, as well as viewing the outputs as they are realised.

Analysis of the phenomena and identification of measure for reducing inequalities between countries and within them (e.g. https://www.istat.it/storage/rapporti-tematici/sdgs/2022/goal10.pdf).

Study on the impact of social inequalities on post-pandemic dropout:
Students who come from disadvantaged families are the most prone to school dropout. A relationship, that between starting inequalities and school performance, whose impact also needs to be analyzed at the local level. The data analyzed are the basis for data-driven policies to address inequalities resulting from school dropout.
https://www.openpolis.it/limpatto-delle-disuguaglianze-sociali-sulla-dispersione-dopo-la-pandemia/#12-gli-studenti-di-famiglie-svantaggiate-che-nel-2022-non-hanno-raggiunto-competenze-adeguate-il-doppio-dei-coetanei-avvantaggiati

RESPONSE TO THE REVIEWER
The study is an elaboration of OpenPolis Foundation which collect and process data to tell stories and produce original analysis, reports and surveys.

A regional equity profile to assess the impact of social inequalities on determinants and health outcomes in the population residing in Sicily Region (Southern Italy). Is a descriptive study aimed to define an equity profile in Sicily by using a rich list of indicators of structure of the resident population and of distribution of determinants and health outcome, derived from the integration of available information and scientific evidence at regional level with high local detail.
The equity profile collects available information on the health status of the population in Sicily, on the determinants, and on the use of health and social services. The characteristics of people or population groups have been explored and can produce inequalities on health which included individual and context socioeconomic status. Using available information sources and study results have explored the effects of the disadvantage on health in the region: mortality, morbidity, oncological incidence, reproductive health, and some of their determinants.
The study highlights how from the use of available information sources and the results of regional studies that have explored the effects of health disadvantage, several health outcomes (mortality, morbidity, cancer incidence, reproductive health and some of their determinants) have been characterized from an equity perspective.
https://epiprev.it/articoli_scientifici/un-profilo-di-equita-regionale-per-la-valutazione-dellimpatto-delle-disuguaglianze-sociali-sui-determinanti-e-sugli-esiti-di-salute-nella-popolazione-residente-in-sicilia

In this case data is used to provide evidences and as basis to the impact assessment of social inequalities.

Multiannual Financial Framework 2021-2027 Dataset. The Multiannual Financial Framework defined by the European Commission with the resources allocated to EU member states for the period 2021-2027, divided into expenditure headings.
[ https://www.rgs.mef.gov.it/VERSIONE-I/e_government/amministrazioni_pubbliche/igrue/BancheDati/CatalogoOpenData/index.html ]

Osservatori RRN Ismea: Competitiveness indicators - Socio-economic context
This section contains the indicators that describe the socio-economic context in which Italian agriculture is set.
In particular, the socio-economic context is described through dashboards on the territory, population, per capita GDP (at current value or purchasing power parity), employment rate (also distinguished in female and male), unemployment rate (overall and youth).
In the economy and employment dashboard, it is possible to consult the variables employment, labour productivity and added value referring to the macro-sectors of the economy: total economy, primary, secondary and tertiary sectors; there is also a dashboard dedicated to investment (gross fixed capital formation and the ratio of investment to added value), again broken down by macro-sectors. In these last two dashboards, in addition to the data in absolute value, those on the % composition of the value of the total economy by macro-sector are available.
Finally, information on household consumption expenditure is available in this section, both overall and for agri-food-related expenditure items: food and non-alcoholic beverages, alcoholic beverages, tobacco and narcotics, hotels and restaurants. Here too, in addition to data in absolute value, the composition of expenditure by individual item is available.
[ https://www.ismeamercati.it/osservatori-rrn/indicatori-competitivita/contesto-socio-economico ]

RESPONSE TO THE REVIEWER
Based on the data published, it has promoted the creation of a series of Observatories on some peculiar characteristics of Italian agriculture. The Observatories were thus created with the aim of systematically collecting and cataloging data and information of a different nature that can be useful tools for understanding the various phenomena affecting the agricultural world.
Through the website it is possible to visit the thematic Observatories on "Youth Entrepreneurship" and "Female Entrepreneurship".
